distinguishing_features: A physical bonded compliant PU/nylon-PU lining on the pipeline flow surface, rather than a software predictor from motor-current/temperature logs.
Erosion mitigation through increased particle-contact duration, impedance mismatch, and hysteretic energy dissipation rather than through calculated remaining-life thresholds.
Specific treatment of sliding bed-load contact at the pipe bottom with a 15-30 mm sacrificial lining and mechanical keying to the steel wall.
Failure management by maintaining a replaceable liner barrier ahead of the pipe MRT rather than by estimating impeller erosion dose from RMS current deviation.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce material loss of a hydrotransport pipeline wall exposed to sliding particulate bed load while keeping the solution installable and inspectable in service.
parsed.viable_reason: A bonded 15-30 mm PU/nylon-PU liner is a practical, inspectable sacrificial barrier that can shield the steel from particle contact and reduce transmitted peak contact forces, despite the simplified stress model.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 1 teaches only a current/temperature-based erosion-life predictor and supplies no teaching or motivation to use a compliant sacrificial pipe lining or contact-time/hysteresis stress attenuation for sliding bed-load erosion.
